author: Jambowlyai
text:
Some questions as I'm really not getting it despite a lot of reading on the forum.

So the engulf told you that price wanted to go up?

Then you wait for a retrace to get in?

You saw that the demand at the DBR/FTR had not been been consumed yet so
 you figured that would be a good place to enter? Did you know that
price would go here?

The DBR at the most recent swing low might be a good place for a later entry as it would act as a cap on price?

The FTR target is a good target because price would have to enter a new
PAZ to go any higher which there is a lower probability of?

Some more questions, an FTR is an FTR until it's high/low is exceeded?
But the chances of it working in your favour decrease with every time
price dips in to find supply/demand?

Does the engulf of a FL have more significance than the engulf of a high/low?

Thanks for any assistance you (or anybody else) may be able to give.

author: Hotochin
text:
Jam,

I don't think IF will mind if I answer some of your questions. I was
actually talking about this with someone else one this forum. Think of
FTR's as the flag limits. I have attached a chart with engulfs and the
following flag limits marked with purple arrows. Notice how price "stair
 steps its way up?" When one of the limits gets engulfed that is your
clue as to where price wants to go! When a whole zone gets engulfed you
will be amazed at how price will respect them on the way down. Notice
how price is compressed while in the zones? I think the trick is to
watch the extremes of these zones and look for PA on smaller time frames
 for confirmation.

Good luck,

H
